answer: He could qualify if he is under age 21 with an emotional disturbance or serious emotional disturbance plus at least one risk factor in the last 12 months. Running away from home or placements or threatening to run away on one or more occasions counts as a risk factor, which must be documented on the Certification of Eligibility and in his treatment plan. The passages do not state whether his specific foster placement will approve or arrange the referral.

citations.quote: The recipient must meet the diagnostic eligibility criterion described in Section A and also meet at least one of the risk factors in Section B.
The recipient is under the age of 21 years and has an emotional disturbance or a serious emotional disturbance.
The recipient must be at risk due to one of the following factors in the last 12 months:
Has run away from home or placements or threatened to run away on one or more occasions.
The recipient’s risk factor(s) must be documented and detailed on the Certification of Eligibility and reflected in the recipient’s treatment plan.

gold_answer: Possibly. He must be under 21 and have an emotional disturbance or serious emotional disturbance, and he must also have at least one of the listed risk factors in the last 12 months. Running away from home or placements is one of those listed risk factors.

judge.rationale: The answer gives the same conditions as the gold (under 21, emotional or serious emotional disturbance, at least one risk factor in the last 12 months, and running away counts), and every claim, including the documentation requirement, appears in P3.

question: My foster son is 17 and keeps running away from his placement. Could he qualify for behavioral health overlay services?
